title: SDK compatibility layer and examples: streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs across TS/Python/Go
creator: Samira Patel
description: Unify and ship SDK-level compatibility helpers and canonical examples for streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured-output enforcement across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Deliver a small compatibility shim that maps older SDK call shapes to the new Wire Protocol so customers upgrading SDKs (or using language-specific clients) get predictable streaming semantics and built-in structured-output validation.
acceptance_criteria: TypeScript SDK exposes a stable async-iterator based streaming API that emits chunk objects matching the server wire format and includes tool-calling events (tool_request/tool_response)
Python SDK provides both sync generator and async async-generator streaming wrappers; tooling calls surfaced as events and function_result objects in-stream
Go SDK exposes a channel-based streamer and a high-level convenience ReadStream that supports tool invocation hooks
Compatibility layer translates legacy `stream: true` and old `tools` call shapes to the unified function-calling protocol without requiring server changes
Structured-output helpers included: Zod schema (TS), Pydantic model (Py), Go struct tags + runtime check; failing validation surfaces clear error/warning modes (strict/soft) documented
End-to-end examples and unit/integration tests added for each language and included in release notes
Migration guide drafted and reviewed by DX and PM; rollout plan for minor semver increment and deprecation schedule documented
implementation_notes: TS: implement streaming API as async iterator `for await (const chunk of client.streamGenerate(...))` where `chunk.type` in {token, delta, tool_request, tool_response, done}`
TS: provide backward-compatible wrapper `client.generate({stream: true, ...})` -> calls `streamGenerate` and flattens to legacy callback events for customers on older codepaths
Python: expose `client.stream_generate()` returning an async generator; also provide `client.stream_generate_sync()` that wraps an event loop for sync users
Python: use Pydantic v2 models for structured-output validation and allow `mode` flag (strict|soft) so callers can opt to treat validation failures as warnings
Go: streaming via channels `StreamResult` struct with Type and Payload; provide `ReadStream(ctx) io.Reader` convenience adapter for text-only streams
Common: introduce `tool_call_id` correlation field in stream events to match request/response pairs; ensure SDKs surface this for observability
Compatibility: add server-side compatibility header mapping and SDK shim that translates older `tools` arrays into function schema descriptors expected by new function-calling protocol

Testing: integration harness against local dev server using model-mock that emits tool_request sequence and structured JSON outputs; perf smoke test for streaming latency under 200ms median on localhost
examples: TS example: samples/ts/streaming-tool-call.ts — demonstrates async iterator consumption, handling tool_request event and invoking a local tool via SDK helper
TS snippet: `for await (const e of client.streamGenerate({model: 'rwd-7b', prompt})) { if (e.type === 'tool_request') await tools.invoke(e.tool_name, e.arguments) }`
Python example: samples/py/stream_tool_structured.py — shows async generator usage and Pydantic schema enforcement with soft mode fallback
Python sync example: samples/py/sync_stream_adapter.py — uses `client.stream_generate_sync` for Django/Flask apps where async loop is not available
Go example: samples/go/stream_tools/main.go — uses `StreamResult` channel, decodes `tool_request`, calls a local binary, then sends `tool_response` back via client helper
Migration guide: docs/migration/sdk-stream-toolcall-migration.md — maps old parameters to new API, includes code snippets for each language
Compatibility test matrix: tests/compat/compat-matrix.md — shows transformations applied and expected in-stream event sequences
